body:
This pull request introduces several improvements focused on error handling, resource management, and configuration clarity. The main changes include enhancing the robustness of file and resource cleanup, improving error reporting, and updating linter and test configurations for better maintainability and code quality.

**Resource Management and Error Handling:**

* Updated all `defer` statements for file and resource closures to ignore errors safely, preventing potential panics and ensuring resources are always released. This affects files such as `download.go`, `uninit.go`, and `config_add.go`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e15bc8089c5531e27bae3a2e60120949a5fb3396df31abbcdac055e918249d5eL219-R219) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-facc7b113b06af6b8edb9c4d428f468831507d590243609d0dce572ef72d1016L100-R100) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-facc7b113b06af6b8edb9c4d428f468831507d590243609d0dce572ef72d1016L123-R125) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-14bc4ce79abf81a07a96a5dc913988f578339c0d694fa5f02bc02f016bb040acL102-R102)
* Improved error handling for file seeking and synchronization operations, ensuring that errors are reported and handled gracefully. For example, seeking in GPG verification and keyring loading now checks for and returns seek errors, and lock file syncing now cleans up on error. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a12c5c1aa6d1edc4256e94870b10f1d1ca332f68134085170105b94835f084L211-R217) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c1a12c5c1aa6d1edc4256e94870b10f1d1ca332f68134085170105b94835f084L384-R392) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2b5b26b1aebec835a0539a741eaf0d3e25d5340f57289ea2ae6a785fc7abe14cL64-R68)

**Configuration and Linting:**

* Refined `.golangci.yml` to clarify linter settings: set default linters to none, increased cyclomatic complexity threshold, added explicit gosec exclusions, and improved test-specific exclusion rules. This enhances code quality and reduces noise from unnecessary warnings. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6179837f7df53a6f05c522b6b7bb566d484d5465d9894fb04910dd08bb40dcc9L2-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6179837f7df53a6f05c522b6b7bb566d484d5465d9894fb04910dd08bb40dcc9L24-R55)

**Test Improvements:**

* Enhanced tests to check and report errors for file operations and HTTP writes, making tests more robust and easier to debug. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L52-R54) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L101-R105) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L131-R137) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L158-R166) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L219-R229) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L257-R269) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L292-R306) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L324-R340) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L333-R351) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L342-R362) [[11]](diffhunk://#diff-49d4a94dfc77699befec5f86653f0293114a6c0945717c9e540d6ff3f737c5c6L378-R400) [[12]](diffhunk://#diff-c734f070f78f35aec9af883af0a152daa5e02b1211e95ce7d3948b63c7743f85L444-R448)
* Updated test setup and teardown to use error-checked environment variable changes and context-aware function calls, improving reliability and correctness. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c734f070f78f35aec9af883af0a152daa5e02b1211e95ce7d3948b63c7743f85R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c734f070f78f35aec9af883af0a152daa5e02b1211e95ce7d3948b63c7743f85L605-R608) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c734f070f78f35aec9af883af0a152daa5e02b1211e95ce7d3948b63c7743f85L637-R640)

* Simplified and clarified error messages, especially for transaction recovery instructions, making them more concise and user-friendly.

**Miscellaneous:**

* Fixed a bug in path normalization test by using `strings.HasPrefix` instead of `filepath.HasPrefix`, ensuring correct behavior. author: moonejon
body:
## Summary
This PR hides the notes feature from unauthenticated users and non-owners viewing public reading lists. Previously, anyone viewing a public reading list could see note indicators on books and access the notes editing interface, even though they couldn't actually save notes. This change ensures notes-related UI elements are only visible to the list owner.

## Changes Made

### BookDetailModal Component
- Added `isOwner` prop to component interface
- Wrapped notes textarea section in conditional rendering (`{isOwner && ...}`)
- Hid "Save Notes" button for non-owners
- Hid "Remove from List" button for non-owners
- Non-owners now only see book details and a "Close" button

### BookCard Component  
- Added `isOwner` prop to component interface (defaults to `true` for backward compatibility)
- Wrapped notes indicator icon in conditional rendering
- Notes indicator badge no longer appears for non-owners even if notes exist

### BookGrid Component
- Added `isOwner` prop to component interface
- Passed `isOwner` prop to all `BookCard` instances (both desktop drag-and-drop grid and mobile static grid)

### ReadingListDetailScreen Component
- Passed `isOwner` prop to `BookGrid` component
- Passed `isOwner` prop to `BookDetailModal` component

## Privacy & UX Improvements
- Non-owners can no longer see that notes exist on books (no visual indicator)
- Non-owners cannot access the notes editing interface
- Reduces confusion by hiding features that require ownership
- Maintains privacy of personal notes from public viewers

## Test Plan
- [ ] View a public reading list as an unauthenticated user - verify no notes indicators appear
- [ ] View a public reading list as an authenticated non-owner - verify no notes indicators appear
- [ ] Click on a book in a public list as a guest - verify notes section is hidden in detail modal
- [ ] View your own reading list as owner - verify notes indicators still appear
- [ ] Edit notes on your own list - verify all notes functionality still works
- [ ] Verify remove button is hidden for non-owners in book detail modal

## Summary by Sourcery

Add week-aware scraping, parsing, and UI selection to align recipes with Planthood’s delivery schedule and support multiple weeks per recipe.

New Features:
- Support multiple delivery weeks per recipe across scraper, parser, scheduler, and site data models.
- Introduce a Playwright-based scraper to build a weekly schedule mapping Planthood delivery weeks to recipe URLs.
- Add a week-aware home page experience with a dropdown to jump between delivery weeks and highlight the current week based on the delivery schedule.
- Add a CLI flag to parse recipes for a specific week and merge results into existing parsed data.
- Schedule an automated weekly GitHub Actions workflow to scrape, parse, and schedule new recipes.

Enhancements:
- Improve week label handling by normalizing various date formats and sorting weeks chronologically rather than lexicographically.
- Update recipe filtering and ordering to work with both legacy single week labels and the new multi-week structure.
- Refine the homepage copy and link users to the official Planthood cooking instructions.
- Enhance styling and responsiveness of the week selector and dropdown controls on the site.
- Ensure scrape and build tasks include the new weekly scraping step and Playwright dependency.

Build:
- Add Playwright as a dependency and wire new scrape-weeks and adjusted build-site tasks into the project task runner.

CI:
- Add a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that runs the weekly scrape, parse, schedule pipeline and commits updated data files.

Chores:
- Add small helper scripts for inspecting Planthood collections and saving HTML snapshots for debugging.

There was [consensus](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/pull/73537#discussion_r2631743951) for `fields` package. - [ ] Validate that such a component can be used well with other use cases like `site logo`, content only controls etc.. - [x] Multiple file selection - [x] Update handling for different media types. - [x] Previews of different media types. Basic implementation is already added (`img` for images and `icons` for the rest), but we might want to improve these. It can also be a follow up. - [ ] Update designs and explore the suggested 'expanded' variant with bigger previews (follow up) ## Testing Instructions 1. In trunk this can only be tested in Featured Image quick edit, in site editor's pages page. Ensure that the Featured Image field is working properly. 2. You can test both media handling by enabling/disabling the `Data Views: new media modal` GB experiment. 3. We cannot have storybook examples because this component needs a WP instance, so in order to make some manual testing you can update the Featured Image field's [Edit](https://github.com/WordPress/gutenberg/blob/trunk/packages/fields/src/fields/featured-image/index.ts#L18) and `setValue` to something like: ``` Edit: ( props ) => , setValue: ( { value } ) => ( { featured_media: value ?? 0, } ), ``` This code would allow any file types and also multiple selection. You can test combinations with the above by adding specific `allowedTypes` and/or removing `multiple`. Noting that the with the above code the `save` won't work properly (unless it's a single image), because we're hijacking the `featured image` post's value. It should be enough to test the UI/UX though. ## Recording The above snippet for multiple files and multiple allowed file types is used for this video. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dca37a93-43b8-471c-b91a-61f9fcf098bc

author: kring
body:
1. Set `CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH`. The vcpkg toolchain will do this itself if it manages to run, but it won't run when cesium-native's `CMakeLists.txt` is `add_subdirectory`'d into another project. By making sure this is set, we avoid the need to set `CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_LIBRARY` and similar to `BOTH` when cross-compiling in order for the build to be able to find the vcpkg dependencies.
2. Detect the triplet as `wasm32-emscripten` if _either_ `CESIUM_TARGET_WASM` is explicitly set, or if the `CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME` is `Emscripten`. This is important when `detect-vspkg-triplet` is invoked from outside cesium-native's top-level `CMakeLists.txt` (e.g., when cesium-native is included via `add_subdirectory`).

Making these fairly reasonable changes here lets us avoid doing hackier things in cesium-unity.

author: chrisurf
body:
# Voice Switcher Feature

This PR adds a comprehensive voice switcher feature that allows users to quickly change voices without opening the settings panel.

## 🚀 Key Features

- **Quick Voice Switching**: Click-to-change voice from status bar (desktop) and control bar (mobile)
- **Context Menu Interface**: Beautiful dropdown menu showing all 25 available voices with checkmarks
- **Real-time Updates**: UI reflects voice changes immediately across all components
- **Automatic Language Detection**: Language codes are automatically set when voices change
- **Cross-platform Support**: Works seamlessly on both desktop and mobile devices

## 🏗️ Technical Improvements

### Centralized Voice Configuration
- Created `VoiceOption` interface with structured voice data (`id`, `label`, `lang`)
- Centralized all 25 voices in `VOICES` array in `VoiceSettings.ts`
- Eliminated hardcoded voice lists scattered throughout codebase

### Enhanced AWS Polly Integration
- `setVoice()` now automatically sets correct `LanguageCode` for each voice
- Simplified `getLanguageCode()` using centralized voice lookup
- Improved SSML synthesis reliability with proper language mapping

### User Interface Enhancements
- **Desktop**: Clickable voice display in status bar with context menu
- **Mobile**: Voice switcher button in mobile control bar
- **Settings**: Dynamic voice dropdown populated from centralized configuration
- **Accessibility**: Added proper ARIA labels for screen readers

## 📱 User Experience

**Before**: Users had to open Settings → Voice to change voices  
**After**: Single click from status bar or mobile controls for instant voice switching

## 🧪 Code Quality

- **DRY Principle**: Eliminated code duplication across components
- **Type Safety**: Proper TypeScript interfaces for all voice data
- **Maintainability**: Adding new voices requires only updating the `VOICES` array
- **Consistency**: Unified voice handling across desktop and mobile platforms

## 📊 Changes Summary

- **5 files changed**
- **+123 insertions, -81 deletions**
- **Net: +42 lines**

## 🧩 Files Modified

- `src/settings/VoiceSettings.ts` - Centralized voice configuration
- `src/service/AwsPollyService.ts` - Enhanced voice/language mapping
- `src/settings/VoiceSettingTab.ts` - Dynamic voice dropdown
- `src/utils/IconEventHandler.ts` - Desktop voice switcher
- `src/utils/MobileControlBar.ts` - Mobile voice switcher

## 🎯 Testing

This feature enhances existing functionality without breaking changes. All voice selection methods continue to work, with the addition of new quick-access options.

---

This enhancement significantly improves user workflow while maintaining clean, maintainable code architecture.

User requested documentation on how to run RSBuilding model locally for semantic segmentation (建筑物提取和变化检测).

### Changes

- **`tools/inference.py`** - New inference script supporting:
  - Single-image building extraction

  - Optional overlay visualization output

### Usage

```shell
# Building extraction
python tools/inference.py \
    --config configs_finetune/Swin_T/Swin_T_inria.py \
    --checkpoint /path/to/checkpoint.pth \
    --input image.png \
    --output result.png \
    --task building

python tools/inference.py \
    --config configs_finetune/Swin_T/Swin_T_levircd.py \
    --checkpoint /path/to/checkpoint.pth \
    --input t1.png t2.png \
    --output change.png \
    --task change_detection

# Batch processing
python tools/inference.py \
    --input-dir /images/ \
    --output-dir /outputs/ \
    --task building
```

## Description Video files in the "Colour Mixing - Behind the Scenes" section failed to play in most browsers due to QuickTime/MOV format issues, and were loading extremely slowly due to large file sizes (~170 MB total for 6 videos). This PR adds graceful error handling with fallback UI, updates video paths to reference the newly converted MP4 files, and implements lazy loading with click-to-play for significantly improved performance. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Code refactoring - [x] Performance improvement - [x] Style/UI update ## Related Issue Video Files Analysis - Issues Found ## Changes Made - Added `videoErrors` state to track which videos fail to load - Added `onError` handler on video elements to detect playback failures - Implemented fallback UI with Film icon and "Video format not supported" message - Updated video paths from `/img/mixing/videos/` to `/videos/mixing/` to reference newly converted MP4 files - Updated filenames to match new naming convention with spaces: `Mixing (X).mp4` - Reduced video list to 6 videos matching the available converted files - **Implemented lazy loading to fix slow video loading:** - Changed `preload` to `"none"` to prevent immediate loading of all videos - Removed `autoPlay` - videos now use click-to-play - Added Intersection Observer for lazy loading when videos scroll into view - Added "Click to play" overlay UI with play button icon - Videos only load when user clicks, preventing 6 large videos (~170 MB total) from loading simultaneously ## Screenshots ### Before ### After ## Testing Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] The code builds without errors (`npm run build`) - [x] The code passes linting (`npm run lint`) - [x] The code passes type checking (`npm run typecheck`) - [ ] I have tested on multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) - [ ] I have tested on mobile/tablet devices - [x] No console errors appear - [x] Existing functionality still works correctly ## Additional Notes **Performance Improvements:** The video files are large (12-44 MB each, ~170 MB total). Previously all 6 videos tried to auto-load simultaneously, causing extremely slow page loads and some videos failing to load. Now videos use lazy loading with click-to-play: - Page loads instantly without waiting for videos - Only the video the user wants to watch is loaded - Much better mobile and low-bandwidth experience **Videos now supported:** - ✅ `Mixing (5).MP4` - ✅ `Mixing (10).mp4` through `Mixing (14).mp4` The error fallback UI remains in place as a safety net for any playback issues. ## Checklist - [x] I have read the [CONTRIBUTING](../CONTRIBUTING.md) guidelines - [x] My code follows the project's coding standards - [ ] I have updated the documentation (if applicable) - [x] My changes generate no new warnings or errors - [x] I have added comments to complex code sections - [x] My commit messages are clear and descriptive

AI agents are increasingly being used to help maintain and update documentation. Without proper guidance, AI agents may:

## Motivation

<!-- Describe your motivation why you will submit this PR. This is useful for reviewers to understand the context of PR. -->

Suppose the nominal range of parameter x is [L, U] and the noise range is ±ε. If x is near the bounds, its robustness depends on how the objective function behaves outside the nominal range.

In the worst-case scenario, the objective function value may be favorable near the bounds, but deteriorate sharply when moving outside the bounds. Since we are seeking robust parameters, we should not select such x. But, to learn such behavior of the objective function,  it is necessary to be able to sample values outside the nominal range.

## Description of the changes

<!-- Describe the changes in this PR. -->

To achieve this, the `noisy_suggestion` option is added, which makes`suggest_float()` return values with added noise rather than nominal values.

In this case, since the range specified for `suggest_float()` should be the range after adding noise, the `nominal_ranges` option is added to specify nominal ranges separately.

body:
---

**Update – Mock AOI Pipeline (Backend + UI)**

**Server / Backend:**

* Added a **mock AOI pipeline** for `Set AOI` behind the route: `POST /api/v1/projects/mock-set-aoi/:projectId`.
* Pipeline runs **6 realistic stages** aligned with the future real flow:

  * Create 1,000m buffer
  * Clip data
  * Merge data
  * Set buffer
  * Assign group
  * Calculate indices
* For now, these stages do **not run the real business/spatial queries**. Each stage only executes **very simple `find` / `count`-style queries** on existing tables (`projects`, `project_polygons`, `en_green`) to simulate load and timing:

  * e.g. `findByPk`, `findAll` with limits, `count`, etc. (no data mutations / heavy processing yet).
* Emits Socket.IO events for live status:

  * `aoi:pipeline_started` – when the pipeline starts
  * `aoi:pipeline_stage` – per stage with step number, label, and success/failure
  * `aoi:pipeline_completed` – final status (`success`, `failed`, or `partial_failure`) + summary
* Introduced `AOI_MOCK_SIMULATE_FAILURE` env flag (`true|false`) to optionally force a controlled failure in one stage so the UI can handle error states.
* Extracted pipeline logic into a dedicated file: **`services/mockpipelineservice.js`** so `projectService` stays focused on core CRUD and polygon handling.

**UI / Frontend:**

* Wired the **Set AOI** button in `AoiRightPanel` to call the mock route and subscribe to the AOI Socket.IO events via `SocketContext`.
* While the pipeline is running:

  * The **Set AOI** button is **disabled**.
  * A spinner + **stage counter** is shown to the right of the button (e.g. `0/6 → … → 6/6`).
* After completion:

  * Shows a **green check icon** on full success.
  * Shows a **red error icon** on failure / partial failure.
* In the **LeftPanel project list**, added per-project AOI status indicators:

  * Spinner next to the project name while its pipeline is running.
  * Green check on success; red error icon on failed/partial pipelines.
* AOI pipeline state is tracked in Redux (`aoiPipeline` slice), so navigating away and back keeps the status in sync.

author: gregpriday
body:
## Summary

Refactor `WorktreeMonitor.ts` to use atomic state updates instead of sequential emissions. This eliminates the visible "staggered" effect in the UI where file counts update before summaries, creating a flickering experience.

Closes #196

## Changes Made

- Extract `fetchLastCommitMessage()` helper returning string without side effects
- Refactor `updateGitStatus()` into 8-phase atomic update cycle (fetch-then-commit pattern)
- Add `startTrafficLightTimer()` for timer-only operations
- Fix traffic light timer race condition when transitioning to clean state
- Move AI summary trigger to fire-and-forget after main emission
- Deprecate `handleSummaryUpdate()` - logic now inline in `updateGitStatus()`
- Rewrite tests for atomic update behavior and polling-based approach

## Implementation Notes

**Context & rationale:**
- Current implementation emits multiple state updates during a single polling cycle
- This causes UI flickering where file counts update before summaries
- Goal: Single atomic state update per polling cycle using Fetch-Then-Commit pattern

**Implementation details:**
- Extracted `fetchLastCommitMessage()` helper that returns string without side effects
- Refactored `updateGitStatus()` into 8-phase atomic update cycle:
  1. Fetch Phase: Get git status
  2. Detect Changes: Hash-based comparison
  3. Prepare Draft: Draft all state values before committing
  4. Handle Summary: Fetch last commit synchronously when clean (THE FIX)
  5. Update Mood: Compute before atomic commit
  6. Atomic Commit: Apply all state changes at once
  7. Single Emission: One `emitUpdate()` call
  8. Post-Emit Async: AI summary fires after main emission
- Added `startTrafficLightTimer()` for timer-only operations
- Updated `triggerAISummary()` to be clear fire-and-forget with own emission
- Deprecated `handleSummaryUpdate()` - logic now inline in `updateGitStatus()`

## Follow-up Tasks

- Pre-existing test failures in `tests/services/ai/worktree.test.ts` - unrelated to this PR
- Optional future enhancement: centralized polling in WorktreeService (not implemented)

author: clumsynonono
body:
This commit addresses several issues to improve the accuracy and maintainability of the codebase:

## Fixes

1. **Accurate liquidation profit calculation** (aave-client.ts)
   - Fixed profit calculation to properly account for liquidation mechanics
   - Correctly handles the relationship between debt paid and collateral received
   - Formula: max liquidatable debt = min(debt * 0.5, collateral / (1 + bonus))
   - Profit = liquidatable debt * bonus percentage
   - Resolves edge cases where collateral is insufficient

2. **Improved risk level classification** (aave-client.ts)
   - Clarified risk levels: HIGH (hf < 1.0), MEDIUM (1.0 <= hf < 1.02), LOW (1.02 <= hf < 1.05)
   - Added comment to indicate the LOW risk range
   - Previous logic had unreachable else branch

3. **Better error handling in batch operations** (aave-client.ts, types.ts)
   - Added BatchAnalysisResult interface with error field
   - batchAnalyzeLiquidation now returns error information for failed addresses
   - Users can see which addresses failed and why
   - Fixed issue where totalChecked count was misleading

4. **Fixed numeric precision issues** (index.ts)
   - Replaced manual bigint conversion with ethers.formatUnits()
   - Prevents precision loss for very large numbers (> 2^53)
   - More consistent with the rest of the codebase

5. **Improved code quality in batch statistics** (index.ts)
   - Separated statistics calculation from object initialization
   - Clearer, more maintainable code structure
   - Added 'successful' and 'failed' counts to summary
   - Included error messages in batch results

All changes maintain backward compatibility while providing more accurate data and better error visibility.

body:
This commit fixes critical and medium priority dashboard issues:

## P0: Race Condition in Dashboard Loading (CRITICAL) Problem:
- loadDashboard() started stats and portfolio in parallel
- portfolio calculated PnL using cachedTotalInvested = 0
- cachedTotalInvested only set AFTER portfolio completed
- Result: Wrong PnL shown on first load/refresh

Fix:
- Await loadStats() FIRST to populate cachedTotalInvested
- Then load portfolio (now uses correct cached value)
- Portfolio and history still load in parallel for speed

Impact: Dashboard now shows correct PnL on first load

## P2: UI Confusion (Total vs Net Invested)
Problem:
- UI showed "Total Invested: €1,000"
- But PnL used net_invested (€500 after sells)
- User confused why numbers don't match

Fix:
- Added "Total Sold: €X" field
- Added "Net Invested: €X" field (highlighted in blue)
- Now shows complete picture:
  * Total Invested: €1,000 (total buys)
  * Total Sold: €500 (total sells)
  * Net Invested: €500 (used for PnL) ← clear!

## P2: No SELL History
Problem:
- /api/history filtered to only show BUYs
- Manual sells invisible in dashboard

Fix:
- Backend: Include both BUY and SELL in history API
- Frontend: Show sells with red background/text
- Frontend: Show buys with green background/text
- Visual indicators: "BUY" or "SELL" badge on each trade

Changed "Recent Purchases" → "Recent Trades" to reflect new scope

## Technical Changes
Files modified:
- app.py: /api/history now returns all trades (buy+sell)
- dashboard.js: Fixed loading sequence, added sell styling
- index.html: Added total_sold and net_invested fields

Result: Dashboard is now bulletproof and user-friendly

**Verification Methods and Rules:**

* Removed all references and schema definitions for the `SigningCertificate` verification method, including its usage in lists, rules, and OpenAPI schema definitions. body:
🛠 DevTools 🛠

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/Miaoxiang-philips/mlflow/pull/19024?quickstart=1) #### Install mlflow from this PR ``` # mlflow pip install git+https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow.git@refs/pull/19024/merge # mlflow-skinny pip install git+https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow.git@refs/pull/19024/merge#subdirectory=libs/skinny ``` For Databricks, use the following command: ``` %sh curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlflow/mlflow/HEAD/dev/install-skinny.sh | sh -s pull/19024/merge ```

### Related Issues/PRs Related #18613 ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? MLflow's OTLP/HTTP traces ingestion currently does not support any compression format. OpenTelemetry Collector sends OTLP/HTTP requests using gzip compression by default, which causes MLflow to return: ``` error": "not retryable error: Permanent error: rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = error exporting items, request to http://host.docker.internal:5000/v1/traces responded with HTTP Status Code 400", "dropped_items": 1} ``` This PR adds support for the required OTLP/HTTP compression encodings: - gzip (required by OTLP specification) - deflate - identity (default) The server now automatically decompresses the request body before parsing the protobuf payload. This makes MLflow compatible with all standard OTLP/HTTP exporters without requiring the user to disable compression. This change does not affect any existing functionality and maintains full backward compatibility. **Reproduce steps**: 1. prepare opentelemetry-collector.yaml: ``` receivers: otlp: protocols: http: endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318 exporters: otlphttp: endpoint: http://host.docker.internal:5000 # if running otel collector by docker, This can be connect to localhost:5000 headers: x-mlflow-experiment-id: "0" # default id service: pipelines: traces: receivers: [otlp] exporters: [otlphttp] ``` 2. start otel collector by docker ``` docker run --name otel-collector -d -p 4318:4318 -v $(pwd)/opentelemetry-collector.yaml:/etc/otel/collector/config.yam otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib # latest tag or 0.139.0(in my environment) ``` 3. send data with otlp If you don't have a ready-made method, you can use `telemetrygen` to simulate data transmission, for example: ``` telemetrygen traces \ --otlp-http http://localhost:4318 \ --rate 10 \ --duration 30s \ --otlp-insecure ``` telemetrygen download link: [telemetrygen package](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/cmd/telemetrygen) ### How is this PR tested? - [ ] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests - [x] Manual tests ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. You can skip the rest of this section. - [ ] Yes. I've updated: - [ ] Examples - [ ] API references - [ ] Instructions ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [ ] No. You can skip the rest of this section. - [x] Yes. Give a description of this change to be included in the release notes for MLflow users. #### What component(s), interfaces, languages, and integrations does this PR affect? Components - [ ] `area/tracking`: Tracking Service, tracking client APIs, autologging - [ ] `area/models`: MLmodel format, model serialization/deserialization, flavors - [ ] `area/model-registry`: Model Registry service, APIs, and the fluent client calls for Model Registry - [ ] `area/scoring`: MLflow Model server, model deployment tools, Spark UDFs - [ ] `area/evaluation`: MLflow model evaluation features, evaluation metrics, and evaluation workflows - [ ] `area/gateway`: MLflow AI Gateway client APIs, server, and third-party integrations - [ ] `area/prompts`: MLflow prompt engineering features, prompt templates, and prompt management - [x] `area/tracing`: MLflow Tracing features, tracing APIs, and LLM tracing functionality - [ ] `area/projects`: MLproject format, project running backends - [ ] `area/uiux`: Front-end, user experience, plotting, JavaScript, JavaScript dev server - [ ] `area/build`: Build and test infrastructure for MLflow - [ ] `area/docs`: MLflow documentation pages #### How should the PR be classified in the release notes? Choose one: - [ ] `rn/none` - No description will be included. The PR will be mentioned only by the PR number in the "Small Bugfixes and Documentation Updates" section - [ ] `rn/breaking-change` - The PR will be mentioned in the "Breaking Changes" section - [ ] `rn/feature` - A new user-facing feature worth mentioning in the release notes - [x] `rn/bug-fix` - A user-facing bug fix worth mentioning in the release notes - [ ] `rn/documentation` - A user-facing documentation change worth mentioning in the release notes #### Should this PR be included in the next patch release? `Yes` should be selected for bug fixes, documentation updates, and other small changes. `No` should be selected for new features and larger changes. If you're unsure about the release classification of this PR, leave this unchecked to let the maintainers decide.

author: susilehtola
body:
This PR implements an instantiated interface to external programs, accessible in C or Fortran.

Right now, it only implements spin-restricted calculations without symmetry, but extending to symmetry and other types of wave functions will be straightforward once we nail down the interface.

The big questions here are
- how to pass in parameters to OOO? This is essentially related to #4, and the best solution likely is to get rid of the individual setters and getters and instead just have a `std::map<std::string,std::any>` to store the various data.
- how to generalize the plugin infrastructure such that it is easier to access various variables in OOO? This again is likely easiest to handle with a `std::map<std::string,std::any>` which is already used in the C++ callback; we just need to figure out how to enable getting values one by one.

body:
Conducted high-level and low-level security audit of the FlashFusion Commerce Forge application as requested.

## Audit Report (`SECURITY_AUDIT.md`)

### High-Level Findings
- **Architecture**: React/TypeScript/Vite/Supabase stack with clean separation of concerns
- **Auth**: Supabase Auth with hCaptcha, role-based access control (admin/moderator/user)
- **Database Security**: RLS policies implemented across tables with multi-tenant support
- **Error Handling**: Comprehensive logging with edge functions and alert system

### Low-Level Findings
- **Code Quality**: 22 ESLint errors (mostly `no-explicit-any`), 12 warnings
- **Dependencies**: 9 npm vulnerabilities (3 low, 5 moderate, 1 high)
- **Test Coverage**: None

### Critical Issues Identified

**1. Privilege Escalation in `bootstrap_admin`**
```typescript
// Any authenticated user can grant themselves admin
const { error } = await supabase.rpc('bootstrap_admin', {
  target_user: user.id
});
```
Recommended fix: Add guard to only allow when no admins exist.

**2. Wildcard CORS in Edge Functions**
```typescript
const corsHeaders = {
  'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*', // Should restrict in production
};
```

### Recommendations Summary
| Priority | Item |
|----------|------|
| Critical | Fix bootstrap_admin, run `npm audit fix` |
| High | Restrict CORS, add TypeScript types, add tests |
| Medium | Rate limiting, CSP headers |

  - Check if folder/file still exists and isn't trashed

  - Order search results by createdTime (oldest first)
  - Always use the oldest folder (most likely to have data)

--- AGENTS.md (root) ---
# Agents

Purpose

This repository uses automated agents (AI assistants, Dependabot, CI bots, etc.) to help with code, documentation, and dependency management. This document explains which agents are commonly used, how their contributions should be reviewed, and the expectations for maintainers when accepting changes produced by an agent.

Which agents we use

- GitHub Dependabot: automatic dependency updates.
- GitHub Actions: CI/CD workflows and automated release workflows.
- AI assistants (Copilot / copilot): used by contributors when drafting code or docs. These are not autonomous contributors — humans are ultimately responsible for content.
- Other bots (labeler, stale bot, etc.) as configured in .github/workflows or .github/*.

How we treat agent contributions

- Treat agent-generated content like any other contribution: review for correctness, security, license, and style.
- For dependency updates (Dependabot): verify CI passes, review changelog / release notes for breaking changes, and run a local smoke test if necessary.
- For AI-assisted code or docs: ensure a human reviewer validates the changes. Do not accept changes that introduce unclear intent, security issues, or licensing problems.

Review checklist for agent-created PRs

- Does CI pass? (unit tests, linters, type checks)
- Is the change small and well-scoped?
- Are there any secrets, tokens, or sensitive data accidentally added?
- Are dependency updates pinned to safe versions and tested?
- Documentation: is the content accurate, and does it match the repository's docs conventions?
- If AI-assisted: check for hallucinated facts, incorrect code assumptions, or missing context.

Security and secrets

- Agents must never commit secrets or credentials.
- If an agent PR contains secrets, immediately close the PR and rotate any exposed secrets.
- Use repository secrets and Actions masked variables for CI.

When to approve and merge

- Approve only when the review checklist is satisfied.
- Prefer squash merging small, single-purpose agent PRs.
- For larger updates, consider a staged roll-out or an incremental approach.

Questions

If you have questions about an agent's change or want to adjust repository agent settings, open an issue or contact the maintainers.

--- end AGENTS.md (root) ---

--- docs/AGENTS.md ---

body:
##### SUMMARY

closes #229

Add functionality to the `proxmox_snap` module to allow users to list all snapshots for gven VM or container. This information can then be used by a user to delete specific snapshots using the `state: absent` calls.

**Issue:** https://github.com/ansible-collections/community.proxmox/issues/229

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
proxmox_snap

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
Currently, the `proxmox_snap` module supports creating, removing, and rolling back snapshots, but it does not provide a built-in way to list existing snapshots. Adding `list_snapshots: true` allows a task to return all snapshots for a VM or container in a structured format.  This list can then be used to remove multiple specific snapshots for a VM or container.

Example usage:
```yaml
- name: List all snapshots for container or VM
  community.proxmox.proxmox_snap:
    api_user: root@pam
    api_password: password123
    api_host: node1
    vmid: 100
    list_snapshots: true
```

author: nongjossss-commits
body:
Modified the `app:check-expiries` command to ensure it correctly respects the `is_enabled` flag for all notification types defined in the admin settings.

Previously, the command only checked the `is_enabled` flag for `pink_card_missing` and `residence_permit_missing` notifications. Other notification types (e.g., passport expiry, visa expiry, employer documents) were generated regardless of their status in the settings.

This change adds a check for the `is_enabled` property on the `NotificationSetting` model before creating any notification. This ensures that when an admin disables a specific notification type, the system will no longer generate alerts for it, aligning the application's behavior with the configured settings.

author: danielvartan
body:
Hi @giacfalk,

This PR adds several changes to the package, including some discussed in issue #3.

I know this covers a lot, but while studying and using the package for a project on allocating fresh and healthy food facilities in Brazil (you can see the pipeline [here](https://cem-usp.github.io/locais-nova-location-allocation/)), I ran into several areas that needed improvement. These changes bring the package in line with the best R practices and clear all R CMD check issues. You can also preview the proposed documentation site [here](https://danielvartan.github.io/locationallocation/).

Independently of this pull request, I’d like to offer to join as a coauthor. I can assist with code review, prepare the package for [rOpenSci](https://ropensci.org/pt/) peer review, and help move it toward [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/). I also noticed your plan to submit the package to [JOSS](https://joss.theoj.org/). The rOpenSci review can [fast-track the review process](https://devguide.ropensci.org/softwarereview_intro.html#whysubmit:~:text=rOpenSci%20packages%20that%20are%20in%20scope%20for%20the%20Journal%20of%20Open%2DSource%20Software%20and%20add%20the%20necessary%20accompanying%20short%20paper%2C%20would%2C%20at%20the%20discretion%20of%20JOSS%20editors%2C%20benefit%20from%20a%20fast%2Dtracked%20review%20process.), potentially speeding up the JOSS submission.

For context: I’m a developer at [rOpenSci](https://ropensci.org) and the author of several R packages, three of which are on CRAN. You can find more about my work on my [GitHub](https://github.com/danielvartan/).

Again, this offer is independent of this contribution. I think the package has real value and can support important work.

Here’s a summary of the changes:

- Refactored the codebase for better maintainability.
- Fixed R-CMD-check issues.
- Added [`checkmate`](https://mllg.github.io/checkmate/) for defensive programming.
- Added [`cli`](https://cli.r-lib.org/) for improved command line interface, including progress bars.
- Added [`lintr`](https://lintr.r-lib.org/) and updated the code to follow the [tidy tools manifesto](https://tidyverse.tidyverse.org/articles/manifesto.html), the [tidyverse design principles](https://design.tidyverse.org/), and the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/).
- Added [`spelling`](https://docs.ropensci.org/spelling/) for spell checking.
- Added [`testthat`](https://testthat.r-lib.org/) for unit testing.
- Added the [Contributor Code of Conduct v3](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/3/0/code_of_conduct/) to incentive contributions.
- Added `CITATION.cff` and `codemeta.json` files for better citation and metadata.
- Added a `NEWS.md` file to track changes to the package.
- Added an R-CMD-check GitHub Action workflow.
- Added default values to `allocation()`, `allocation_discrete()` and other functions.
- Added the demo data as documented exports, and changed their names to: `naples_shape`, `naples_population`, `naples_fountains`, and `naples_hot_days`.
- Changed the theme of [`ggplot2`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) plots to `theme_minimal()` with customizations.
- Changed `allocation_plot()` to have `0` as a lower limit for the color scale.
- Merged `allocation_plot()` and `allocation_plot_discrete()` into a single `allocation_plot()` function.
- Changed `allocation()` and `allocation_discrete()` to raise an error when the initial coverage is greater or equal to the `objectiveshare` parameter.
- Improved code efficiency and performance.
- Improved documentation and examples for all functions.
- Removed `demo_data_load()`, as it is no longer necessary.
- Removed the `fasterize` dependency due to compatibility issues with Linux systems.
- Updated `_pkgdown.yml` for better pkgdown site generation.
- Updated package dependencies to their latest versions.
- Updated README documentation and added badges for R-CMD-check, DOI, license, and Contributor Code of Conduct.

And a "to do" list:

- Add a contributor guide.
- Add references to function documentations and data sources.
- Add test coverage (Codecov).
- Add unit tests.
- Conduct a thorough review of all algorithms.
- Document the data.
- Improve documentation.
- Merge `allocation` and `allocation_discrete`.
- Move to the [r-spatial](https://r-spatial.org/) framework or adopt the [`terra`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra) package (the first option aligns better with tidyverse principles).
- Reduce cyclomatic complexity.
- Standardize parameter names (for example, `updatevalue` to `new_value`).
- Update the hex logo.

Thank you for your excellent work!

Cheers! :)

body:
The `sparkdock` command was missing service restart steps that `sjust http-proxy-install-update` performed manually after Ansible provisioning, causing inconsistent http-proxy management behavior. ## Changes ### Ansible Playbook (`ansible/macos/macos/base.yml`) - Added "Restart http-proxy service" task block under `http-proxy` tag - Checks Docker daemon availability with `docker info` (not just CLI presence) - Executes `spark-http-proxy start` to restart service (which handles container cleanup via Docker Compose) - Handles Docker unavailability gracefully ### Just Recipe (`sjust/recipes/00-default.just`) - Removed redundant post-Ansible Docker cleanup and service restart - Both commands now execute identical logic through Ansible ```yaml - name: Restart http-proxy service tags: http-proxy block: - name: Check if Docker daemon is running command: docker info register: docker_check changed_when: false failed_when: false - name: Start http-proxy service command: spark-http-proxy start when: docker_check.rc == 0 ``` Both `sparkdock` (all tags) and `sjust http-proxy-install-update` (http-proxy tag only) now restart the service consistently through the same Ansible task. The `spark-http-proxy` command handles all container management including cleanup via Docker Compose, so no explicit `docker rm` is needed. - Fixes sparkfabrik/sparkdock#292
Original prompt > > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > [Feature]: Align command `sparkdock` with `sjust http-proxy-install-update` > ### Feature Description > > When running `sparkdock` multiple actions are executed. One of them handles the `http-proxy`. We also have a dedicated command with `just` called `sjust http-proxy-install-update` that only handles the update of `http-proxy`, which is handy when someone want to manually refresh it. > > ### Problem or Use Case > > The problem is that these two commands are not 100% aligned in terms of actions that they execute. Specifically: > > | Aspect | `sparkdock` | `sjust http-proxy-install-update` | > |--------|------------|-----------------------------------| > | Git update logic | ✅ Yes (via Ansible) | ✅ Yes (explicit with stashing) | > | Repository configuration | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | > | Symlink creation | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | > | Docker cleanup | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | > | Service restart | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | > | Runs other system tasks | ✅ Yes (all tags) | ❌ No (http-proxy only) | > > `sparkdock` includes the http-proxy installation/update logic but **doesn't restart the service**. The `sjust http-proxy-install-update` command is more comprehensive for http-proxy updates because it explicitly restarts the Docker container, which `sparkdock` does not do. > > ### Proposed Solution > > So given this overview, the goal would be to find the best and cleanest way to align the `sparkdock` command with the logic from `sjust http-proxy-install-update`, while also keeping the rest of the `sparkdock` logic intact. In other words the two missing steps: "Docker cleanup" and "Service restart". > > Also make sure that there aren't any extra actions/steps that we might have missed from the `sjust http-proxy-install-update` command. > > ### Alternatives Considered > > _No response_ > > ### Implementation Ideas > > _No response_ > > ### Would you like to contribute this feature? > > Yes, I'd like to implement this > > ### Additional Context > > _No response_ > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > >

author: davidw-philips
body:
<!-- Provide a brief description of your changes -->
Adds in-memory locks to prevent race conditions in mcp-server-memory that caused file corruption and "Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON" errors

## Description

Solves the following issue: Bug Report and Resolution: mcp-server-memory Failures due to Race Condition and Environment Misconfiguration #2579

The memory server had no protection against concurrent file writes. When multiple operations tried to read, modify, and write to the `memory.jsonl` file simultaneously, they would corrupt the file causing JSON parsing errors. This fix implements a Promise-based in-memory lock manager that serializes all file operations, ensuring atomic read-modify-write cycles without data loss or corruption.

## Server Details
<!-- If modifying an existing server, provide details -->
- Server: memory
- Changes to: Core file operation logic and locking mechanism

## Motivation and Context
<!-- Why is this change needed? What problem does it solve? -->

The memory server was experiencing critical failures when handling concurrent tool invocations:
1. **Race Condition**: Multiple concurrent read-modify-write operations on `memory.jsonl`
2. **File Corruption**: Interleaved writes resulted in truncated JSON lines
3. **Data Loss**: Some writes would completely overwrite others
4. **JSON Parse Errors**: "Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON" when reading corrupted files

This was particularly problematic when Claude made multiple memory operations in quick succession or when the server handled rapid concurrent requests. The fix ensures all operations are properly serialized while maintaining high performance through JavaScript's asynchronous Promise-based queue system.

## How Has This Been Tested?
<!-- Have you tested this with an LLM client? Which scenarios were tested? -->

Comprehensive testing with vitest including:
- **Race Condition Prevention Tests** (5 tests): Concurrent entity/relation creation, high-concurrency scenarios, mixed read/write operations
- **Lock Verification Tests** (6 tests): Serialization verification, JSONL format integrity, atomic operation verification
- **Existing Tests**: All 30 original knowledge graph tests continue to pass
- **Coverage**: 82.69% statement coverage, 97.46% branch coverage, 94.73% function coverage

Total: **50/50 tests passing** with no regressions

## Breaking Changes
<!-- Will users need to update their MCP client configurations? -->

No breaking changes. The fix is transparent to users:
- Same API and tool signatures
- Same file format (JSONL)
- No configuration changes required
- Backward compatible with existing `memory.jsonl` files

## Types of changes
<!-- What types of changes does your code introduce? Put an `x` in all the boxes that apply: -->
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update

## Checklist
<!-- Go over all the following points, and put an `x` in all the boxes that apply. -->
- [x] I have read the [MCP Protocol Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
- [x] My changes follows MCP security best practices
- [x] I have updated the server's README accordingly
- [x] I have tested this with an LLM client
- [x] My code follows the repository's style guidelines
- [x] New and existing tests pass locally
- [x] I have added appropriate error handling
- [x] I have documented all environment variables and configuration options

## Implementation Details

### Changes Made

1. **Lock Manager Implementation** (`src/memory/index.ts`):
   - Added `LockManager` class using Promise-based queue for per-file serialization
   - All file operations wrapped with `executeWithLock()` to ensure atomicity
   - No external dependencies required (removed `proper-lockfile`)

2. **Test Suite Enhancement**:
   - Created `race-condition.test.ts` with 5 comprehensive concurrent access tests
   - Created `lock-verification.test.ts` with 6 lock mechanism verification tests
   - Both follow vitest standards per CONTRIBUTING.md requirements
   - Removed Python test files in favor of TypeScript equivalents

3. **Dependencies**:
   - Removed: `proper-lockfile` and `@types/proper-lockfile`
   - Added: None (uses built-in Promise-based async/await)

### How It Works

The `LockManager` maintains a Map of Promise chains, one per file. When an operation is requested:
1. Get the current lock promise for the file (or start with resolved Promise)
2. Chain the new operation to that promise
3. Store the updated promise chain for future operations
4. This ensures operations execute sequentially without data corruption

### Performance Considerations

- **No blocking**: Uses JavaScript's asynchronous Promise queue, not OS-level blocking
- **Minimal overhead**: Simple Map lookup and Promise chaining
- **Efficient**: Operations complete faster due to serialization (no partial writes)
- **Scalable**: Works for single instance deployments (intended use case)

## Additional Context
<!-- Add any other context, implementation notes, or design decisions -->

### Architecture Notes

The fix assumes a single MCP server instance, which is the standard deployment model for MCP servers. The in-memory Promise-based lock provides optimal performance for this scenario while preventing all race conditions within a single process.

**⚠️ Important: This is a Temporary Measure for Single Editor Usage**

This implementation is designed for users running **one code editor/LLM client at a time** (e.g., Claude Desktop, VS Code, or CLI - but not multiple simultaneously). If you use multiple LLM clients or editors concurrently with the same memory file, you may still experience race conditions.

### Multi-Client Scenarios

If you need to use multiple LLM clients/editors simultaneously (e.g., Claude CLI + Gemini CLI + VS Code all at the same time), you should implement one of the following production-ready locking strategies:

#### Option 1: SQLite Database (Recommended)
- **Library**: Use `better-sqlite3` or built-in Node.js SQLite support
- **Advantages**: ACID transactions, process-safe, no external dependencies
- **Implementation**: Replace JSONL storage with SQLite tables
- **Example**:
  ```typescript
  import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
  
  const db = new Database('memory.db');
  // Transactions handle all locking automatically
  db.exec('BEGIN TRANSACTION');
  // ... read and write operations ...
  db.exec('COMMIT');
  ```

#### Option 2: Redis with Atomic Operations
- **Library**: `redis` npm package
- **Advantages**: Distributed locking, multi-machine support, battle-tested
- **Implementation**: Store graph in Redis with Lua scripting for atomic operations
- **Example**:
  ```typescript
  const client = redis.createClient();
  // SET with NX (only if not exists) for locks
  const acquired = await client.set('memory:lock', '1', { NX: true, EX: 30 });
  ```

#### Option 3: Filesystem Locks with Retry Logic
- **Library**: `proper-lockfile` (production-ready version) or `fs-ext`
- **Advantages**: No external services required, cross-process safe
- **Implementation**: Use OS-level file locks with exponential backoff
- **Note**: Requires careful error handling and timeout management

#### Option 4: Message Queue Pattern
- **Library**: Bull, RabbitMQ, or Apache Kafka
- **Advantages**: Serializes all operations globally, scalable
- **Implementation**: Queue all graph operations through a message broker
- **Use Case**: Large-scale systems with many concurrent clients

### Recommendations by Use Case

| Use Case | Recommendation | Rationale |
|----------|---|---|
| Single editor (Claude Desktop or VS Code) | Current in-memory locks ✓ | Optimal performance

body:
Reworked the CTA on recipe cards: replaced generic “Learn more” inside a nested <button> with a single semantic <Link> that:

reuses existing button styles via className={${link} ${button}},

renders a descriptive label like View recipe: Shakshuka instead of a repeated “Learn more”.

Added an explicit aria-label="View recipe: {title}" to recipe links to improve screen-reader experience and make link purpose unambiguous.

Removed the anti-pattern <button> inside <Link>, simplifying the markup and avoiding nested interactive elements while preserving the existing visual design.

Introduced a reusable NotFoundLayout wrapper for not-found screens with support for both Image and SvgIcon illustrations, error code, message text and a “Back to Home” action.

Styled the not-found layout to match the design: centered content, responsive illustration with the same proportions as the original 600×438 image, and mobile/desktop spacing tweaks.

Aligned the “Back to Home” link styling with the global outlined button pattern (hover/focus/active transitions and box-shadow focus ring) for consistent a11y and interaction states.

Ensured that the recipe “not found” page uses the shared layout and can be reached via an invalid /recipes/:id URL for testing and demos.

body:
This pull request refines the PowerShell script in the `updatePackageVersion.yml` workflow to improve reliability and clarity when selecting and updating a NuGet package version. The changes enhance error handling, add helpful debug output, and clarify the version selection logic.

**Improvements to package version selection and script robustness:**

* Refactored the script to use local variables (`$packageName`, `$targetVersion`) for better readability and maintainability, and replaced the empty string check with `[string]::IsNullOrEmpty` for more robust handling of missing parameters.
* Improved error handling by checking for missing search results and matching packages, with informative messages and early exits if no results are found.
* Added debug output to show the number of total and matching packages found, and to list all matching versions, making troubleshooting easier.
* Clarified and simplified the logic for selecting the latest matching version, ensuring the script reliably picks the newest version according to SemVer 2.0, including pre-releases.

**Minor corrections:**

* Fixed a typo in a comment from "package propery element" to "package property element" for clarity.

body:
Adds newsletter subscription, contact form, and dynamic statistics APIs with corresponding frontend pages to enhance user engagement and platform functionality.

## Changes

### Backend APIs
- **Newsletter** (`/api/newsletter/`) - Subscribe, unsubscribe with secure tokens, preferences update, stats
- **Contact** (`/api/contact/`) - Form submission with ticket ID generation, categories endpoint
- **Statistics** (`/api/stats/`) - Platform metrics, trending topics, daily quotes, upcoming events

### Frontend
- **Newsletter page** - Subscription form with interest selection, frequency options, live stats
- **Contact page** - Multi-category form, FAQ accordion, character counter
- **Homepage enhancements** - Newsletter widget, animated stat counters, daily quote, dropdown nav

### Security & Reliability
- Rate limiting on all endpoints (5/hr subscribe, 30/min general, 3/hr contact)
- Email validation, input sanitization, length limits
- Full demo mode when no database connected
- RGPD-compliant consent flows

// Example: Newsletter subscription with rate limiting
router.post('/subscribe', subscriptionLimiter, async (req, res) => {
    const { email, interests, frequency } = req.body;

    }
    // Demo mode fallback when no DB

        return res.json({ success: true, demo: true });

});

author: rustopian
body:
[WIP]

This addresses Issue https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/issues/235, fixing two issues with the [original](https://github.com/anza-xyz/solana-sdk/pull/257) (reverted) PR:

1. The contract of `from_raw_parts_mut` was being violated, in a way that miri considered safe, but which could have theoretically caused trouble in the future.
2. The implementation assumed that the number of bytes returned by the runtime was exactly
`mem::size_of::<Self>()`, which was not always true. `Rent`, for example, contains a `u64`, an `f64` and a `u8`. In memory the compiler pads this struct to 24 bytes, but the runtime stores its contents as a 17‑byte `bincode` serialization. The `get_sysvar` call thus returns only 17 bytes. Passing a 24‑byte buffer results in an `OFFSET_LENGTH_EXCEEDS_SYSVAR` error and undefined behavior when uninitialized bytes are interpreted as f64.

Note: this PR only updates the three sysvars `Rent`, `EpochSchedule`, and `EpochRewards`, which require two different approaches as commented below. `Clock` and `LastRestartSlot` do not require special handling.

Thanks to [jamie-osec](https://github.com/jamie-osec) for investigating the cause here and noticing the `from_raw_parts_mut` violation. I'll add you as contributor to the final.

## Description

This PR updates the versions of the software:

- [Hugo](https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo)
  - From
    - Version: `0.147.5`
  - To
    - Version: `0.152.2` (latest supported by Blowfish v2.92.0)
- [Blowfish theme](https://github.com/nunocoracao/blowfish)
  - Fast-forwarded from
    - Version: `v2.86.0`
    - Commit ID: `0b06a64139beba6287e7685f4c810ad4ff772fde`
    - Timestamp: `Tue May 27 01:03:33 2025 +0100`
  - Fast-forwarded to
    - Version: `v2.92.0`
    - Commit ID: `81f0e887100f4ddc9856c6d662883b62ab7b1043`
    - Timestamp: `Mon Nov 3 22:34:25 2025 +0000`

### Fixes and improvements from incorporating the Blowfish updates

Incorporating the upstream changes to overridden files brought the following benefits:

- Article cards on the main page don't have random gaps on the bottom edges anymore
- Long summaries in article cards are now trimmed (with ellipses) to the size of the card
- On the right side of the website header, the gap is removed between the right border and buttons/menus
- While scrolling down in an article, the button `Scroll to top` now appears in the bottom-right corner
- The TOCs to the right from an article content have a scroll bar now if the TOC is too long

### Other improvements

- Added badges to README for minimum and maximum supported Hugo versions
- Removed unused overridden files
- Improved Kapa widget welcome message
- Refactored our overrides to BLowfish upstream files

## Background information

As you might know, the `espressif/blowfish` repo is added to our `developer-portal` repo as a submodule in the folder `themes/blowfish/`. Over time, we copied a few Blowfish layout files from `themes/blowfish/layouts/` to `layouts/` and applied some changes. Comparing the files in `themes/blowfish/layouts/` with our overridden versions in `layouts/` revealed considerable updates in the former (submodule).

We usually fast-forward the Blowfish submodule changes once in a few months and only incorporate the upstream changes from `themes/blowfish/layouts/` into respective overridden files if the website fails to build or if we discover critical issues. One of such issues was non-functioning burger menu button fixed in PR [#362](https://github.com/espressif/developer-portal/pull/362).

Although, skipping incorporation of non-critical upstream changes saves our time, it leads to accumulating maintenance debt. Ideally, we need to incorporate the upstream changes to our overriden files at least once a year.

I decided to partially incorporate the upstream changes as this will help us better prepare for implementing our own updates planned for the near future, such as adding the Dark theme and improving the main page.

This time, I did the following:

- Extracted our changes by comparing the `layouts/` files with their repective copies in `themes/blowfish/layouts/` at the time of applying these changes
- Applied the extracted changes to the layout files in Blowfish: `v2.92.0`. This task usually requires considerable efforts in figuring out how to implement the changes as simple copying and pasting is usually not possible.
- Moved some code in overrides to custom partials for better maintainability

As a result, the following files have been updated:

- `layouts/partials/article-link/card-related.html`
- `layouts/partials/article-link/card.html`
- `layouts/partials/footer.html`
- `layouts/partials/head.html`
- `layouts/partials/header/basic.html`
- `layouts/partials/hero/basic.html`
- `layouts/partials/toc.html` (removed as it has no overrides)
- `layouts/_default/baseof.html`
- `layouts/_default/single.html`

With these updates, the website builds stably. No major bugs have been identified so far.

author: kamcnally
body:
This PR adds support for Anthropic's Claude models as an LLM provider in paperless-gpt.

I've recently started using paperless-ngx and paperless-gpt but I wanted to use Antropic's API instead of OpenAI etc. I added support for it and have been running for a few days with great results.

I also saw issue #477 requesting the same thing. I think this PR would be a good step forward to addressing that feature request. I've listed some requirements from that below:

| Requirement | Status | Notes |
|------------|--------|-------|
| API key configuration | Complete | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable with validation |
| Model selection | Complete | Supports all Claude models via `LLM_MODEL` / `VISION_LLM_MODEL` - All Claude 3 and 4 models [ref](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision)  |
| Temperature and parameter controls | Complete | Uses existing parameter configuration from langchaingo |
| Rate limiting configuration | Complete | Integrated with existing rate limiting framework |
| Messages API support | Complete | Uses langchaingo's Anthropic provider |
| Error handling and retry logic | Complete | Leverages existing error handling patterns |
| Streaming support | Future Enhancement | Follows same pattern as other providers (no streaming) |
| Token counting/usage tracking | Future Enhancement | Would benefit entire project, not Anthropic-specific - outside scope of initial work IMO |

## Changes Made

### Core Integration
- Added `anthropic` as a new `LLM_PROVIDER` option for document classification
- Added `anthropic` as a new `VISION_LLM_PROVIDER` option for OCR processing
- Implemented Anthropic client creation in both main LLM and vision LLM paths
- Added `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable with validation
- Integrated rate limiting for Anthropic API calls (both vision and standard)

### Configuration & Documentation
- Updated `README.md` with Anthropic configuration examples
- Added environment variable documentation for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
- Updated provider validation to include `anthropic` option

### Testing
- Added unit tests in `ocr/anthropic_provider_test.go`
   - Tests cover: API key validation, client creation, provider initialisation, and configuration options
- Added E2E test in `web-app/e2e/anthropic-ocr-processing.spec.ts`
   - Use the Mistral tests as a base for this with minor alterations to:
      - give more time for the 5-page OCR
      - be forgiving on the text comparison from OCR - I'll comment directly on this in the code

## Configuration Example
```yaml
environment:
  # For document classification
  LLM_PROVIDER: "anthropic"
  LLM_MODEL: "claude-sonnet-4-5"
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: "your_anthropic_api_key"
  
  # For OCR/Vision
  OCR_PROVIDER: "llm"
  VISION_LLM_PROVIDER: "anthropic"
  VISION_LLM_MODEL: "claude-sonnet-4-5"
```

body:
## Summary

This PR consolidates and reorganizes CI/CD documentation by clearly defining the roles of `CI/` and `INFRASTRUCTURE/` directories, eliminating duplications, and improving cross-references.

### Key Changes

#### 📁 File Movements
- `docs/INFRASTRUCTURE/CI_CD_QUICK_REFERENCE.md` → `docs/CI/CI_CD_QUICK_REFERENCE.md`
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT/CI_CD_TESTING.md` → `docs/CI/CI_CD_TESTING.md`

#### 🎯 Directory Role Clarification

**CI/ Directory** - **Daily Operations for Developers**
- Target: All developers working with PRs and CI/CD
- Content: Daily operations, quick references, best practices
- Files: CI_CD_GUIDE.md, CI_CD_TESTING.md, CI_CD_QUICK_REFERENCE.md, CI_CD_BEST_PRACTICES.md, TYPE_GENERATION.md

**INFRASTRUCTURE/ Directory** - **Architecture & Advanced Operations**
- Target: DevOps, infrastructure engineers, project maintainers
- Content: Architecture details, advanced configuration, maintenance
- Files: CI_CD_OVERVIEW.md, CI_CD_CONFIGURATION.md, CI_CD_OPERATIONS.md, CI_CD_TROUBLESHOOTING.md

#### 📝 Content Consolidation
- Removed troubleshooting duplication from `CI_CD_GUIDE.md`
- Added cross-reference headers to all CI/CD documents
- Replaced duplicated content with reference links
- Updated all internal links in moved files

#### 📚 Documentation Updates
- Completely rewrote `docs/CI/README.md` with clear role definitions and usage guide
- Updated `docs/README.md` to reflect new CI/CD structure
- Fixed all broken links caused by file movements

## Root Cause Analysis

**Problem**: CI/CD documentation was scattered across multiple directories with unclear roles, leading to:
- Heavy duplication (troubleshooting, operations, commands)
- Unclear separation between CI/ and INFRASTRUCTURE/
- CI_CD_TESTING.md in wrong directory (DEVELOPMENT/ instead of CI/)
- Maintenance burden due to multiple sources of truth

**Solution**: 
- Establish clear directory roles (daily ops vs. architecture/advanced)
- Move files to appropriate locations based on target audience
- Eliminate duplications through cross-references
- Create comprehensive directory READMEs

**Prevention**:
- Document update policy in CI/README.md
- Clear role definitions prevent future misplacements
- Single source of truth for each topic

## Test plan

- [x] Verify all moved files exist in new locations
- [x] Check all internal links are updated correctly
- [x] Confirm no references to old file paths remain
- [x] Run `npm run ci:lint` - ✅ Passed
- [x] Run `npm run ci:type-check` - ✅ Passed
- [x] Verify documentation structure matches docs/README.md

### Manual Verification
- [x] CI/README.md displays correctly with new structure
- [x] docs/README.md reflects updated file locations
- [x] Cross-reference links work correctly
- [x] No broken links in consolidated documents

## Benefits

✅ **Clear Separation**: Daily operations (CI/) vs. Architecture/Advanced operations (INFRASTRUCTURE/)
✅ **Reduced Maintenance**: Single source of truth for each topic
✅ **Easier Navigation**: Developers know to check CI/ first, INFRASTRUCTURE/ for deep-dives
✅ **No Information Loss**: All content preserved and better organized
✅ **Improved Discoverability**: Better README files guide users to correct documents

Closes #301

author: egorpopelyaev
body:
…s` (#10362)

While triaging the Versi-net, I've discovered that the connection between collators and validators sometimes takes less than 20ms, while at other times it takes more than 500ms.

In both cases, the validators are already connected to a different protocol. Therefore, opening and negotiating substreams must be almost instant.

The slot timer of the peerset artificially introduces the delay:
- The `SetReservedPeers` is received by the peerset. At this step, the peerset propagated the `closedSubstream` to signal that it wants to disconnect previously reserved peers.
- At the next slot allocation timer tick (after 1s), the newly added reserved peers are requested to be connected

This can introduce an artificial delay of up to 1s, which is unnecessary.

To mitigate this behavior, this PR:
- Transforms the ` enum PeersetNotificationCommand` into a structure. Effectively, the peerset can specify directly to close some substreams and open other substreams
- Upon receiving the `SetReservedPeers` command, peers are moved into the `Opening` state and the request is propagated to the litep2p to open substreams.
- The behavior of the slot allocation timer remains identical. This is needed to capture the following edge cases:
- The reserved peer of the `SetReservedPeers` is not disconnected, but backoff / pending closing.
  - The reserved peer is banned

cc @paritytech/networking

Detected during versi-net triaging of elastic scaling: https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/issues/10310#issuecomment-3543395157

### Problem
User input validation currently lacks a reliable method to verify email formats. 
This results in inconsistent behavior across modules requiring email checks.

### Expected Behavior
A single reusable function should validate:
- Basic email structure
- Allowed characters
- Presence of domain and extension

### Actual Behavior
Several components manually check email patterns, leading to duplicated logic and potential validation gaps.

### Fix Implemented
This PR adds `validate_email.py` containing `is_valid_email()` which:
- Uses a standard regex pattern
- Safely handles non-string inputs
- Returns a boolean result for easy integration

### Additional Notes
This utility will be used in upcoming form-handling improvements.

1. Add additional check after the check of bucket policy by principal ARN of the user to also check the permission in account level.
2. Fix `permission_by_arn` call to `has_bucket_policy_permission` so the last argument will be an object.

### Issues: 
List of GAPs:
1. This code does not handle a case where there is a user under an OBC account, in case we decide to add this layer.
3. The tests are only manual at this point; there is a plan to add automated tests after we have the design change.

### Testing Instructions:
1. Build the images and install the NooBaa system on Rancher Desktop (see [guide](https://github.com/noobaa/noobaa-operator/blob/master/doc/dev_guide/deply_noobaa_on_minikube_or_rancher_desktop.md)).
_Note: `nb` is an alias that runs the local operator from `build/_output/bin` (alias created by `devenv`)._
2. Wait for the default backing store pod to be in state Ready before starting the tests: `kubectl wait --for=condition=available backingstore/noobaa-default-backing-store --timeout=6m -n test1`
4. I'm using port-forward (in a different tab):
- S3 `kubectl port-forward -n test1 service/s3 12443:443`
- IAM `kubectl port-forward -n test1 service/iam 14443:443`
5. create 2 accounts:
- `nb account create shira-acc01 -n test1 --show-secrets`
- `nb account create shira-acc02 -n test1 --show-secrets`
6. Create the alias for the accounts:
`account-1-s3='AWS_ACCESS_KEY=<access-key> AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<secret-key> aws --no-verify-ssl --endpoint-url https://localhost:12443'`
`account-2-s3='AWS_ACCESS_KEY=<access-key> AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<secret-key> aws --no-verify-ssl --endpoint-url https://localhost:12443'`
`account-2-iam='AWS_ACCESS_KEY=<access-key> AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<secret-key> aws --no-verify-ssl --endpoint-url https://localhost:14443'`
7. Check the connection to the endpoint:
- try to list the buckets: `account-1-s3 s3 ls; echo $?` `account-2-s3 s3 ls; echo $?`
8. Create a bucket for each account:
- `account-1-s3 s3 mb s3://buc-acc1`
- `account-2-s3 s3 mb s3://buc-acc2`
7. Create a user under account 2: `account-2-iam iam create-user --user-name Robert`
Note: To validate user creation, you can run `account-2-iam iam list-users` and expect 1 user in the list
9. Create access keys: `account-2-iam iam create-access-key --user-name Robert`
10. Add IAM policy to the user: `account-2-iam iam put-user-policy --user-name Robert --policy-name policy_allow_s3 --policy-document file://~/Documents/iam-tests/iam_policies/policy_allow_s3.json`

policy_allow_s3.json
```json
{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
        {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
                "s3:*"
            ],
            "Resource": "*"
        }
    ]
}
```
11. Create the alias for the user (like in step 5 with alias `user-2-s3`): `alias user-1-s3='AWS_ACCESS_KEY=<access-key> AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<secret-key> aws --no-verify-ssl --endpoint-url https://localhost:12443'`
12. The case with no bucket policy, for example:
- The user cannot put an object in the bucket in the second account:
`echo 'test_data' | user-1-s3  s3 cp - s3://buc-acc1/test_object.txt` (should not work)
- The user cannot list objects in the bucket (to check the flow of the RPC call of `has_bucket_action_permission` function that was created in the `auth_server`):
`user-1-s3 s3 ls s3://buc-acc1` (should not work)
13. Find the ID of account 2 for the ARN, for example by running: `account-2-s3 s3api get-bucket-acl --bucket buc-acc2` and taking the ID.
14. Add bucket policy of the root account user as principal:
`account-1-s3 s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket buc-acc1 --policy file://policy_principal_arn_owner.json`

policy_principal_arn_owner.json
```json
{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
        {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Principal": {
                "AWS": [
                    "arn:aws:iam::69259fff8b07c200228c4fb3:root"
                ]
            },
            "Action": [
                "s3:*"
            ],
            "Resource": "*"
        }
    ]
}
```

15. The case no bucket policy, for example:
- The user can put an object in the bucket in the second account:
`echo 'test_data' | user-1-s3  s3 cp - s3://buc-acc1/test_object.txt` (should work)
- The user can list objects in the bucket (to check the flow of the RPC call of `has_bucket_action_permission` function that was created in the `auth_server`):
`user-1-s3 s3 ls s3://buc-acc1` (should not work)

Code changes for testing:
1. To see the account (of a user) in the cache after changes, `src/sdk/object_sdk.js` uses cache expiry of 1 millisecond.
```diff
const account_cache = new LRUCache({
    name: 'AccountCache',
-    expiry_ms: config.OBJECT_SDK_ACCOUNT_CACHE_EXPIRY_MS,
+   expiry_ms: 1, //SDSD 
```

Notes:
- In step 1 - deploying the system, I used `--use-standalone-db` for simplicity (fewer steps for the system in Ready status).


- [ ] Doc added/updated
- [ ] Tests added

Frontend API endpoints hardcoded `https://` with codespace URLs, breaking localhost development when `REACT_APP_CODESPACE_NAME` is unset.

## Changes

- **Updated `useApiData` hook** - Now uses the existing `getApiBaseUrl` function from `utils/api.js` for dynamic URL generation
- **Removed redundant `config.js`** - The `getApiBaseUrl` utility already provides environment-aware URL handling

## Before
```javascript
const endpoint = `https://${process.env.REACT_APP_CODESPACE_NAME}-8000.app.github.dev/api/${path}/`;
```

## After
```javascript
import getApiBaseUrl from '../utils/api';

const endpoint = `${getApiBaseUrl()}/api/${path}/`;
```

The `getApiBaseUrl` function handles the environment check and returns `http://localhost:8000` when `REACT_APP_CODESPACE_NAME` is not set.

Addresses technical debt: unused imports/variables, unescaped JSX entities, and missing React Hook dependencies across the codebase.

## Changes

### Unused Code Removal
- Removed unused imports: `router`, `Slot`, `axios`, `TextInput`, `getPotentialMatches`, `interpolate`, `X`, `Platform`, `ShooterPet`, `Dimensions`, `dayjs`, `AlertModal`, `useAlert`

- Removed stale `console.log` debugging statements and unnecessary `eslint-disable` directives

### ESLint Error Fixes
- Fixed unescaped entities in JSX text (`'` → `'`)

### React Hook Dependency Fixes
- Wrapped async fetch functions with `useCallback` and added to dependency arrays
- Example pattern applied across 12 files:

```tsx
// Before
useEffect(() => {
  if (petId) fetchPetData();
}, [petId]);

const fetchPetData = async () => { ... };

// After
const fetchPetData = useCallback(async () => { ... }, [petId, showAlert]);

useEffect(() => {
  if (petId) fetchPetData();
}, [petId, fetchPetData]);
```

- Moved `MOCK_BREEDING_PAIRS` to module scope to prevent recreation on each render
- Used `_param` naming convention for intentionally unused callback parameters

author: copilot
body:
When `path-wizard --recursive` adds paths to NixOS configuration, it spawns child processes per subdirectory. Each child had its own `nix_backup_created=0` state, causing ~20 backup attempts and permission errors on `/etc/nixos/configuration.nix`.

## Changes

- **Shared timestamp across recursive invocations**: Parent sets `PATH_WIZARD_BACKUP_TIMESTAMP` env var before spawning children; all children use the same timestamp for backup file naming
- **Backup deduplication**: Before creating backup, check if one with the shared timestamp already exists; skip if so
- **Refactor**: Extract `generate_backup_timestamp()` helper to consolidate duplicated logic; use `pid` prefix for process ID fallback for clarity

## Example

```sh
# Before: 16 subdirs = 16 backup files created
path-wizard --recursive --format nix add /path/to/spells
# configuration.nix.wizardry.20251125130611
# configuration.nix.wizardry.20251125130611.1
# configuration.nix.wizardry.20251125130611.2
# ... (16 total)

# After: 16 subdirs = 1 backup file
path-wizard --recursive --format nix add /path/to/spells
# configuration.nix.wizardry.20251125130611
```
